title: Invariant Under Iterated Transitions
statement: Let $R$ be a relation on finite Boolean words, let $T$ assign a finite Boolean word to each pair of finite Boolean words, and let $u$ assign a finite Boolean word to each finite Boolean word. Suppose $R(x,u(x))$ holds for every finite Boolean word $x$, and $R(x,s)$ implies $R(x,T(x,s))$ for all finite Boolean words $x,s$. Then, for every finite Boolean word $x$ and every $i\in\mathbb{N}$, $R(x,s_i)$ holds, where $s_i$ is obtained by applying $s\mapsto T(x,s)$ exactly $i$ times to $u(x)$.

$T$ maps pairs of finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
$u$ maps finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
$R(x,u(x))$ holds for every finite Boolean word $x$
$R(x,s)$ implies $R(x,T(x,s))$ for all finite Boolean words $x,s$
